summary: The US and China extended their October 2025 trade truce in late September 2026, and China delayed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. Tariffs are still high: about 36.5% on Chinese goods into the US and 31% on US goods into China, per a July 2026 Congressional Research Service report. On Oct 9 China and the EU reached an interim understanding to roughly halve Chinese hybrid car exports to the EU over four years, and China will cut duties on about EUR 4 billion of EU goods; EU leaders still have to approve it. China is also pushing into memory chips: CXMT's fifth generation DRAM platform is in mass production and its world share passed 10%, which hit Micron and Korean chipmakers on Oct 12. Chinese large caps are weak, with the Shanghai 50 at a 14 month low. September exports rose 36.3% from a year ago and the monthly surplus hit $133.5 billion (Oct 14), with chip exports up 108.1%. Q3 GDP grew 4.5% (Oct 19), just above forecasts, but shoppers stayed weak and investment fell, so big new stimulus looks less likely. On Oct 22 the CSI 300 closed 20.2% below its June 22 peak, its first bear market since 2020, after 10 straight weekly losses, as AI stocks slid across Asia.
for_you: China matters to you mostly through US names that sell there and through memory supply. AAPL is 'Accumulate on pullback', QCOM is 'Wait' and NVDA is 'Buy zone, wait for the chart' on Oct 15 data. A record trade surplus raises the odds of a new tariff fight before the Jan 10 rare earth deadline, and rising Chinese chip exports back the CXMT worry for MU. Size swings normally and skip memory.

watch.name: Yuan per US dollar
watch.why: The last close found was about 6.71 in early September, near a three and a half year high for the yuan.

watch.name: Shanghai Composite
watch.why: Down about 3% over the past month; the Shanghai 50 hit a 14 month low.

watch.name: US tariff on Chinese goods
watch.why: Average rate per CRS. Any change in the truce moves it.

watch.name: Rare earth export ban delay ends
watch.why: If China lets the delay lapse, US magnet, defense and car supply chains get squeezed.

watch.name: Q3 GDP growth
watch.why: Above the 4.4% forecast; nine month growth 4.6%. Retail sales only about 1.1% in September.

watch.name: CSI 300
watch.why: First bear market since 2020, measured from the June 22 peak, after 10 straight weekly losses (Bloomberg via Yahoo).

exposed.exposure: nearly all revenue from China (company filings, approximate)

exposed.name: Apple
exposed.exposure: about 17% of FY2024 sales from Greater China, and most iPhones are assembled there (FY2024 10-K, approximate)
exposed.how: Hit two ways: Chinese sales and a supply chain that runs through China. The truce extension lowers near term risk.

exposed.name: Qualcomm
exposed.exposure: about 46% of FY2024 revenue billed to China customers (FY2024 10-K, approximate)
exposed.how: Chinese phone makers are its biggest buyers, so trade or export curbs land hard.

exposed.name: Nvidia
exposed.exposure: about 13% of FY2025 revenue from China including Hong Kong (FY2025 10-K, approximate)
exposed.how: US export rules decide which chips it can sell to China.

exposed.name: MP Materials
exposed.exposure: US rare earth producer; China added it to an export control list in June 2026
exposed.how: Gains when China threatens rare earth curbs, since buyers look for non-Chinese supply.

changes.what: The US and China agreed to extend the October 2025 truce, and China pushed its rare earth export ban to Jan 10. That lowers near term risk for US firms that sell in China or buy Chinese magnets.
The People's Bank of China said it will not weaken the yuan to gain a trade edge and will publish more currency data from 2027, ahead of EU trade talks.

China's CXMT said its fifth generation DRAM platform (G5) is in mass production, and it held about 10% of world DRAM in Q2 2026. Memory stocks fell on Oct 12: Micron about 2% premarket, Samsung and SK Hynix more than 4% in Seoul. Separately, the Oct 9 EU-China understanding would roughly halve Chinese hybrid car exports to Europe over four years.
changes.for_you: Skip new MU swings while China adds supply. STLA gains if EU leaders approve the hybrid deal this week; it is not a dashboard setup, so no action.

changes.what: China's September exports rose 36.3% from a year ago (25% in August) and imports about 31%, for a $133.5 billion monthly surplus; chip exports rose 108.1% and exports to the US 39.6% (released Oct 14). The nine month surplus is about $938 billion, which adds to EU and US pressure to rebalance trade.
changes.for_you: No action. Rising Chinese chip exports support the case against new MU swings. AAPL is left out of both lists: strong Chinese trade helps its supply chain, but a trade fight would hurt it.

changes.what: China releases Q3 GDP with September retail sales, factory output and investment at 02:00 GMT on Oct 19; a Reuters poll of 50 economists expects 4.4%, up from 4.3% in Q2 but below the 4.5% to 5% target. September rare earth exports rose 6.7% from a year ago to 4,269.8 tonnes (still down 9.6% for the year), and on Oct 15 the commerce ministry said it will keep easing rare earth licenses for the EU.
changes.for_you: No action this weekend. The GDP number lands Sunday evening Pacific time; a miss would weigh on China names and copper on Monday. More rare earths flowing to Europe trims the scarcity case for MP. BABA and PDD are left out until the number is out.

changes.what: China's Q3 GDP grew 4.5% from a year ago and 1.2% from Q2, above the 4.4% and 1.0% forecasts; growth for the first nine months is 4.6%, inside the 4.5% to 5% target. Factories carried it: September output rose 5.5%, while retail sales rose only about 1.1% and fixed asset investment fell 7.2% for January to September. The statistics bureau said weak domestic demand 'remains prominent', and analysts see less reason for big Q4 stimulus.
changes.for_you: No action. BABA (109.11) and PDD (80.97) are in downtrends with up/down volume under 0.9, and weak shoppers do not help. FCX and SCCO are left out of both lists: factory output is fine, but less stimulus removes a tailwind.

changes.what: On Oct 16 China made companies register before exporting a list of AI, biotech and solar technologies, effective at once, and proposed banning exports of 12 solar manufacturing methods, including advanced wafer, perovskite and tandem cell know how (pv magazine, Geopolitechs). Finished panels are not covered. Public comment runs to Nov 15.
changes.for_you: No action. FSLR is left out of both lists: keeping know how in China protects Chinese makers' lead, but it also slows foreign rivals building plants abroad. Watch the Nov 15 comment deadline as a sign of how hard Beijing plays before the Jan 10 rare earth date.

changes.what: China's CSI 300 entered a bear market on Oct 22, closing 20.2% below its June 22 peak after 10 straight weekly losses, its first since 2020. Analysts pointed to doubts about AI returns and a deadline on Beijing's push to tax offshore trusts, which may have pushed some large holders to sell.
changes.for_you: No action. Chinese ADRs are not on the buy zone list. Selling in China adds to pressure on US chip names with big China sales, such as LRCX, whose China share is set to fall.
